description: Working Together to Keep the Lights on in New York City is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by New York City Office of Long-Term Planning and Sustainability. In the wake of Hurricane Sandy, Con Edison examined the future vulnerability of electrical infrastructure. Based on the results, they took action to increase their resilience. Coverage: New York (2015). The toolkit gives New York as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Despite its seeming invincibility as the nation’s largest and most densely populated urban center, New York City‘s location makes it highly vulnerable to coastal storms. In October 2012, Hurricane Sandy caused unprecedented damage to the electricity system across the city—more than two million people lost electricity during the height of the storm.
